title: Rajkumari bani daasi, phir Mahavir ki pehli shishya?
hooks: Rajkumari se daasi, phir Mahavir ki pehli shishya
Ek katori chawal ne tod diya chhah maah ka upvaas
Raajmahal se zanjeer tak, kaise bani pehli sadhvi?
hook_why: Opens with the stark identity flip — princess to slave to first female disciple — in the first 4 words, matching the 'named entity + shocking outcome' pattern that wins on Shorts.
metaphor: A single rice bowl glowing in dark hands, passing through chains to reach a meditating idol's feet — the bowl is the thread linking every fall and rise.
mechanism: Hook: Identity flip in first 4 words
Fall: War, capture, mother's death, sale into slavery
False hope: Kind merchant adopts, jealous wife tortures
Rock bottom: Chained in dark room, no one to tell
Parallel: Mahavira's 6-month fast, same silent endurance
Climax: Last rice bowl offered, chains fall, fast breaks
Rise: First female disciple, white robes, rajoharan in hand
Lesson: Dukh mein bhi daan ka bhav nahi chhuta
End: Relatable choice question + Jai Jinendra

cast.Vasumati_Chandanbala: Young woman, same face across scenes. Scene 1-2: princess in silk and pearls. Scene 3-9: hair loose, simple cotton, later shaven head, chains on ankles. Scene 10-13: white unstitched sadhvi robes, rajoharan in hand, calm eyes.
cast.King_Dadhivahan: Middle-aged king, gold crown with central jewel, layered necklaces, silk dhoti-angavastram, same face and beard in every scene.
cast.Queen_Dharini: Queen in silk saree, gold ornaments, same face, gentle expression.
cast.Soldier: Armoured enemy soldier, turban, sword at waist, rough features.
cast.Dhanavah: Merchant in cotton dhoti-angavastram, simple turban, kind eyes, same face.
cast.Moola: Merchant's wife in silk saree, gold bangles, sharp eyes, same face.
cast.Mahavira_idol: Only as serene white marble idol in padmasana, eyes half-closed, lion emblem on pedestal, halo of soft gold light. Never as action character.

claims.claim: Chandanbala was originally Princess Vasumati of Champapuri, daughter of King Dadhivahan and Queen Dharini
claims.basis: jainworld.com source: 'There once was a beautiful princess named Vasumati. She was the daughter of king Dadhivahan and queen Dharini of Champapuri.'

claims.claim: She was captured in war, mother died, and she was sold as a slave
claims.basis: jainworld.com source: 'When Vasumati's turn came to be sold as a slave...' and 'Upon hearing this, the queen went into shock and died.'

claims.claim: Merchant Dhanavah bought and freed her, renamed her Chandanbala
claims.basis: jainworld.com source: 'a merchant named Dhanavah happened to be passing by... bought Vasumati, freed her from slavery... They named her Chandanbala'

claims.claim: Merchant's wife Moola cut her hair, chained her, and locked her in a room
claims.basis: jainworld.com source: 'she called a barber to cut off all of Chandanbala's beautiful hair. Then she tied Chandanbala's legs with heavy chains and locked her into a distant room'

claims.claim: She offered her last bowl of rice to Mahavira, breaking his 6-month fast
claims.basis: Kalpasutra tradition and user prompt: 'She offered her last bowl of rice to the Lord, breaking his 6-month fast. Source: Kalpasutra.'

claims.claim: She became the first female disciple (sadhvi) of Mahavira
claims.basis: User prompt and Jain tradition: 'first female disciple of Mahavira' and jainknowledge.com reference to her role in Jainism.

figures.name: Vasumati / Chandanbala
figures.look: Young woman, slender build, warm brown skin, large dark eyes, calm serene face. As princess: long black hair braided with pearls, silk lehenga-choli in deep red and gold, heavy pearl necklaces, gold bangles, bare feet on marble. As Chandanbala: shaven head smooth and pale, plain white unstitched cotton sadhvi robes draped simply, soft white rajoharan whisk broom in right hand, muhpatti mouth cloth tied at neck, iron ankle chains in early scenes, bare feet, hands folded in gratitude or offering.

figures.name: King Dadhivahan
figures.look: Middle-aged man, tall broad shoulders, wheatish skin, trimmed black beard streaked with grey, sharp calm eyes. Wears gold crown with central ruby, silk dhoti in saffron, embroidered angavastram draped over shoulder, heavy gold necklaces, armlets, bare chest, bare feet. Rides chestnut horse, reins in left hand, right hand raised urging flight.

figures.name: Queen Dharini
figures.look: Middle-aged woman, graceful build, fair skin, long black hair loose over shoulders, gentle eyes. Wears white silk saree with gold border, simple gold necklace, gold bangles, bare feet. Draped modestly, hands bound in scene 4, head bowed, expression sorrowful but dignified.

figures.name: Soldier
figures.look: Adult male, muscular build, dusky skin, short cropped black hair, thick moustache, stern face. Wears leather armour over cotton tunic, metal greaves, curved sword at hip, round shield on back, leather sandals. Torch in left hand, right hand gripping queen's arm or gesturing to market.

figures.name: Merchant Dhanavah
figures.look: Middle-aged man, medium build, warm brown skin, kind dark eyes, short grey-streaked beard, calm expression. Wears white cotton dhoti, white angavastram draped over left shoulder, simple white turban, no jewellery, bare feet. Carries cloth bag of coins, right hand extended in payment or blessing.

figures.name: Moola
figures.look: Middle-aged woman, sharp features, fair skin, black hair parted centre and braided, piercing dark eyes. Wears rich silk saree in deep green with gold zari border, heavy gold necklaces, multiple gold bangles, gold anklets, diamond nose ring. Stands with hand on hip or gesturing sharply, expression jealous and commanding.

figures.name: Barber
figures.look: Older man, thin build, dark wrinkled skin, white stubble, downcast eyes. Wears dirty white cotton loincloth, bare chest, bare feet. Holds straight razor in right hand, left hand gripping Chandanbala's hair, crouched low.

figures.name: Auctioneer
figures.look: Middle-aged man, stout build, dusky skin, bald head, thick moustache, loud mouth open. Wears cotton dhoti, bare chest, bare feet, wooden gavel in raised right hand, ledger in left.

figures.name: Mahavir Swami (temple idol)
figures.look: Serene meditating figure carved from smooth white marble, seated in perfect padmasana on ornate marble pedestal with lion emblem carved at front. Bare head of small tight curls, bare unmarked forehead, eyes half-closed, calm face, shrivatsa mark on chest, hands resting in dhyana mudra on lap. Halo of soft gold light behind head. No crown, no jewellery, no weapons.

figures.name: Jain monks and nuns
figures.look: Adult men and women, varied ages, slender builds, calm faces. All heads shaven smooth. Wear plain white unstitched cotton robes draped identically, muhpatti mouth cloths, soft white rajoharan whisk brooms held in right hands. Bare feet. Standing or walking in quiet rows.

figures.name: Devotees
figures.look: Men, women, children of varied ages, warm brown skin, calm faces. Wear simple white cotton garments, dhotis, sarees, kurtas. Bare feet or simple leather sandals. Hands folded or holding prayer beads. Walking slowly in peaceful groups.
